title: skill-update cards explain themselves, and decision diagrams accept every decision id the board accepts
acceptance:
Why. The captain asked on 2026-10-04 for the small known defects to be fixed ("小毛病…都修掉"). Two are in scope here:
- (a) `fm.sh self-update` raises its skill-update card with a title only (bin/fm.sh around 672: `fm-decide.sh --request D-SK-<n> --kind choice --title "skill-update: <skill> - <why> (A adopt it, B leave it)"`), with no details. The captain sees a one-line card with no explanation, no before/after and no option pros and cons. For SK-009, firstmate had to write the details by hand.
- (b) `bin/fm-diagram.sh --decision D-SK-009` dies with 'not a decision id'. Its local `is_decision_id()` (around line 93) accepts only `D-<digits>` and `FM_OWNED_ID`, not the `D-SK-<n>` ids the board and fm-decide accept (T-119's single id grammar).

(a) Every skill-update card is requested with authored details in the same en/zh-TW shape firstmate writes: title, explanation, before, after, outcome, and options A (adopt) and B (leave) with pros and cons. The details are built from the proposal itself: the skill, the reason, and the diff summary or proposed text it already records. They are passed with `--details`. If the proposal lacks a field, the card says so plainly; nothing is invented. Re-raising the same SK keeps its id (existing behaviour).

(b) fm-diagram.sh uses the shared decision-id grammar, the same one fm-decide.sh and the board use. It does not keep a local copy. `--decision D-SK-<n>` renders the three files. Ids the board rejects are still rejected.

Tests (fail first, stubs answering like the real tools, HERDR_ENV=0 in helpers):
- a self-update proposal raises a card whose details have every field in both languages
- fm-diagram renders for D-SK-9 and still refuses a malformed id
Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Workers do not run the suites.
